meta.notes: Batch batch-1, the first delivered batch under requirements/thresholds.md section 5.5. This bundle is a corpus member: it counts toward the corpus target of section 16, it consumes the section 5.5 tier grant, and it may enter samples/ once the five conditions of Phase 1 item 2d are met. It is not a shakedown and claims none of the section 12.4 exemptions. Declared gaps: anchors-unmeasured, attestation-unavailable, calibration-unmeasured, cohort-registry-unprojected, dataset-clearance-absent, discrimination-divisor-understates-trials, fidelity-unverified, held-out-variant-unavailable, levers-unprojected, load-envelope-unexercised, mnist-discrimination-unmeasured, neardup-root-unpinned, oracle-unrun, per-step-cost-anchor-unmeasured, perturbation-kind-batch-size-inapplicable, refinement-loop-unbuilt, retrieval-probe-unrun, threshold-provenance-conflict-12-2-against-12-5, tier-below-frontier-mandate, tier-thresholds-unresolved. Authoring intent only. The declared tier is Baseline under the explicit section 5.5 grant, which names the first batch only and expires at the first verified signed CFER. The grant relaxes no check: it changes the design target and nothing else. Independently, FORGE_VIEW projects an empty lever list, so no lever stands ACTIVE and no slot could anchor a higher tier whatever it realized. The measured tier lives only in the ledger and no number here is evidence. Section 12.5 shape: full run 90 seconds, declared episode ceiling 21600 seconds inside the 172,800 envelope, 9 attempts, 12 graded runs per attempt, per-graded-run budget 200.0 seconds, so the full run occupies 45.0 percent of its budget at a margin of 2.22x. The divisor is graded runs rather than 1 plus the perturbation count, because a ruleset perturbation costs a full tuning study set and section 12.1 names the trials term as the one authors miss; under the section formula this slot would read 8.89x. Cost identity: the client delivery shape of 3 rollouts, one episode each, is 324 training runs and 5.2 GPU-hours. The section 10 statistical rule at 15 rollouts across 2 cohorts is 3240 training runs and 51.9 GPU-hours, and section 12.1 binds the corpus ceiling over the batch total rather than over this slot.

save_checkpoints.reason: No graded obligation reads a checkpoint and the writes dominate the artifact footprint.

torch_compile.reason: Left at the upstream default so the execution mode matches the upstream path. On ogbg that default is what produces the model-eager, loss-compiled asymmetry the runner selects from the base workload name, which is the lever rather than a defect.

params.comparator_reason: The workload class compares with a strict greater-than in has_reached_validation_target, so an at-least comparator would grade a different bar than the class this task reuses.

modifications: Reduced execution path. The mnist_fine_grained workload is pinned and requirements section 1 excludes it from the corpus; section 12.4 admits it for a shakedown.
Self-tuning ruleset pinned as the primary.

Budget axis retained but re-anchored. The graded axis is accumulated submission time in seconds, as upstream measures it, read against the budget the runner enforces for the declared ruleset rather than against the upstream time-to-result normalisation.
Reward replaced. A bounded continuous scalar with a conjunctive task-pass predicate replaces the upstream performance-profile integral.
Scoring path replaced. The verifier parses eval_measurements.csv directly and never calls scoring/score_submissions.py, which does not execute under the harness's own pinned NumPy floor.
Conformance rules compiled. Upstream prose rules are compiled into eighteen deterministic checks over the submitted bytes and the recorded log.
Perturbation set added. Two graded conjuncts with no upstream counterpart.
Per-step cost ceiling added. The upstream benchmark states no ratio bound on per-step compute.
